speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. I hear you have generalized fatigue, mild fever, abdominal pain, and nausea; to narrow down the cause, have you had any recent travel, insect bites, or consumption of undercooked meats? Also, have you noticed any rash, joint pain, or changes in your urine or stool?

speaker: Patient
text: 47-year-old female. The patient describes a 3-week history of generalized fatigue, mild fever, abdominal pain, and nausea. She recalls attending the state fair over a month ago where she tried various regional foods. Recently, she has observed the darkening of her urine, which she believes is due to inadequate water intake. She has a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Acute Hepatitis (likely Hepatitis A from the fair food exposure).

I have noted your 3-week history of fatigue, fever, abdominal pain, nausea, and the concerning darkening of your urine despite hydration. Given your history of attending a state fair and consuming regional foods, I suspect a viral hepatitis infection; please confirm if you have experienced any jaundice (yellowing of eyes or skin) or loss of appetite. REQUEST TEST: Liver_Function_Panel, Hepatitis_Serology, Urinalysis.
